inj_report.short: Pitts brought in four of five targets for 50 yards in the Falcons' 35-13 loss to the Chiefs on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.
inj_report.long: The veteran tight end had a slow start to the day before coming on when the Falcons went especially pass-heavy in the second half. Pitts' fumble, his first of the season, came with just over four minutes remaining in the game after the contest was out of reach, and his catch total was his highest since Week 7. Pitts remains a key complementary option in an Atlanta passing attack that's scuffled of late, and he'll look to bounce back after the Falcons emerge from a Week 11 bye with a Week 12 road matchup against the Vikings on Sunday, Nov. 29.

inj_report.short: Waller caught all three of his targets for 42 yards in Sunday's 35-33 win over the Ravens.
inj_report.long: The veteran tight end was out-produced by second-year player Mitchell Evans, who posted a 5-44-1 line on five targets, but Waller made more of an impact than Tommy Tremble, who caught his only target for 18 yards. With all three members of the trio capable of making a splash in any given week, Waller will be tough to rely on heading into a Week 12 meeting with the Buccaneers.

inj_report.short: Godwin caught three passes for 18 yards on three targets in Sunday's 31-21 loss to the Lions.
inj_report.long: The veteran wideout ran a team-high 41 routes on Baker Mayfield's 44 dropbacks, but Godwin continues to produce very little with his immense playing time. He's been held under 40 receiving yards in eight straight games and has yet to have a 50-yard receiving game this season. Godwin also has zero touchdowns. He's a low-floor, low-ceiling fantasy option headed into next Monday night's date with the Panthers.

inj_report.short: Williams brought in nine of 11 targets for 122 yards in the Commanders' 22-20 win over the Bengals on Monday night.
inj_report.long: The rookie third-round pick managed new career highs across all three components of his receiving line, which also all served as team-best totals Monday. Williams' last two catches of the night were his most critical, as he recorded 22- and 42-yard grabs on Washington's final drive to position Drew Stevens for a game-winning 26-yard field goal. Williams hadn't topped 54 receiving yards in any game after a 64-yard effort in his pro debut in Week 1, but Monday night's breakout could serve as a launchpad to a strong stretch run as the Commanders make a playoff push.

inj_report.short: Bryant caught three passes for 32 yards on four targets in Sunday's 38-24 win over the Raiders.
inj_report.long: The wideout briefly exited the game in the third quarter after he appeared to tweak his previously injured ankle, but Bryant quickly returned and was able to finish out the contest. His four targets were fourth on the team on a day Bo Nix targeted nine different players on 35 pass attempts. The Denver offense spreads the ball around to five different receivers, three tight ends and its running backs most weeks, making it difficult for any of the pass catchers to post big numbers in the box score.

In five games playing alongside Smith, Lemon has just 11 catches for 60 yards. Opportunities should be available against Dallas' porous secondary on Thanksgiving, but it remains to be seen if the unproven QB-WR combo of Joe Milton and Lemon can capitalize on that favorable matchup.

inj_report.short: Higbee caught three of four targets for 17 yards and a touchdown during the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
inj_report.long: Higbee's third and final catch of Sunday's game came late in the second quarter, with the veteran tight end connecting with Matthew Stafford for a five-yard touchdown to give the Rams a 10-6 lead. It was the second touchdown of the season for Higbee, with his first taking place in Week 3 against the Broncos. He's been held to three catches or fewer in each of his last four games, although he's been on the field for at least 50 offensive snaps in three of those contests. The Rams are on bye for Week 11, and Higbee's limited target share will take a hit if Davante Adams (hamstring) is activated from injured reserve ahead of Week 12 against the Packers on Wednesday, Nov. 25.

inj_report.short: Bernard caught six passes for 40 yards on 10 targets in Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Eagles.
inj_report.long: With Michael Pittman (foot) remaining sidelined for Week 11, Bernard retained his every-down role on offense, playing 67 of 71 offensive snaps while leading the team in routes (52) and targets. It was a nice bounce-back game for the rookie after he was held without a catch on three targets against the Bengals in Week 10. Pittman is expected back for Friday's game against the Broncos, but Bernard could keep pacing the team in playing time, especially if DK Metcalf gets disciplined for his latest on-field outburst.

inj_report.short: The Rams are expected to lean more on Mumpfield and the rest of the team's wide receivers in the absence of Puka Nacua (knee/toe), the latter of whom is expected to be sidelined for the remainder of the regular season, Nate Atkins and Jonathan Jones of The Athletic report.
inj_report.long: Nacua is expected to miss "a couple of months" after undergoing surgery Tuesday to repair his MCL, per Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com. With Nacua and Davante Adams (hamstring, IR) sidelined for Week 10 against the Cardinals, Mumpfield operated as the Rams' WR1 for that contest and finished with three catches (on four targets) for 81 yards in a 34-6 win for Los Angeles. The Rams are "hopeful" that Adams will return soon, but if he's not activated from injured reserve ahead of Wednesday's game against the Packers, then Mumpfield would lead Los Angeles' wide receiver group that also includes Tutu Atwell, CJ Daniels and Xavier Smith.

inj_report.short: Andrews caught two of three targets for 14 yards in Sunday's 35-33 loss to Carolina.
inj_report.long: While the veteran tight end showed some instant chemistry with new quarterback Jacoby Brissett last week, Andrews saw his target volume crater in their second game together, as rookie depth TEs Josh Cuevas and Matthew Hibner saw similar usage as pass catchers. Andrews has failed to reach 25 receiving yards in five of his last six games and hasn't scored a TD in seven straight contests, making him a very risky fantasy option in Week 12 against the Texans.

inj_report.short: Dowdle rushed five times for 15 yards and caught four of five targets for 19 yards in Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Eagles.
inj_report.long: Dowdle finished with 34 scrimmage yards for a second consecutive game after racking up 235 scrimmage yards over his preceding four appearances. He had five more yards than Jaylen Warren on two fewer touches in Sunday's loss. Dowdle is poised to retain his spot as the 1B option alongside Warren in Friday's Week 12 home game against the Broncos.

Downs' quick chemistry with Patrick Mahomes is certainly noteworthy and makes an already impressive air attack all the more effective heading into Thursday night's Thanksgiving road showdown against the Bills.

The wide receiver has operated in a limited role on offense since DJ Moore returned to action in Week 8 following a shoulder injury, and Coleman will remain an unattractive fantasy asset ahead of the team's matchup with the Chiefs on Thanksgiving night.

inj_report.short: Raymond caught one of four passes for 14 yards during Sunday's 21-13 win over the Saints.
inj_report.long: Raymond's four targets were tied with Rome Odunze for most on the Bears on Sunday, although the former could muster only a 14-yard grab early in the second quarter. Raymond has commanded four targets or more in six of 10 regular-season games and is up to a 33-304-1 line on 45 targets while operating as Chicago's WR3 behind Odunze and Luther Burden. The Bears will hit the road to face the Lions on Thanksgiving Day.

inj_report.short: Sutton didn't corral either of his two targets during Sunday's 38-24 victory versus the Raiders.
inj_report.long: Sutton thus was blanked in the box score for the first time Week 7 of the 2024 campaign, a span of 39 games (including playoffs). Considering he's surpassed 50 receiving yards just one time in 10 appearances in 2026, he doesn't hold much sway for fantasy purposes, especially in a Broncos offense that often has sputtered this season. Sutton's next chance to turn the tide arrives Friday at Pittsburgh.

inj_report.short: Freiermuth caught all five of his targets for 39 yards during Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Eagles.
inj_report.long: Freiermuth matched his season high in catches, securing five passes in a game for the third time this year. The tight end has yet to exceed 50 receiving yards in a contest this season, and he entered Week 11 with exactly two catches in each of the team's last four games. Freiermuth has now caught 32 of 43 targets for 309 yards and five touchdowns while also adding four rushes for five yards and a score over 10 contests so far during the 2026 season.

inj_report.short: Douglas caught one of three passes for four yards during the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions on Sunday in Munich.
inj_report.long: The Patriots' offense was effective on the first drive of the game, but that was where the good news ended for New England after Drake Maye was knocked out for the rest of the contest due to an ankle injury. Tommy DeVito took over under center, and the offense struggled to move down the field for the rest of the game. For Douglas, it was the third time this season that he was held to one catch, with the last instance taking place in Week 3 against the Jaguars. A.J. Brown -- who was cleared to return from a two-game absence due to knee and ankle injuries -- also picked up a hamstring injury during Sunday's game, so Douglas could be the New England's WR1 following the Week 11 bye. The Patriots' next game takes place in Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

inj_report.short: Ayomanor caught all three of his targets for 27 yards in Sunday's loss to Dallas.
inj_report.long: Ayomanor logged season highs with five catches, 10 targets and 79 yards against Jacksonville in Week 10, but he reverted back closer to his usual numbers versus the Cowboys. The second-year wideout did rank third on the team in receptions and receiving yards, and his 37 offensive snaps also were third behind Carnell Tate (62) and Chimere Dike (54). Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) is out for the remainder of the season, but Ayomanor may be hard-pressed to put up reliable fantasy production as the third pass-catching option, at best, for one of the league's least prolific air attacks.

inj_report.short: Johnston caught one of two targets for nine yards in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Jets. He added one yard on one rushing attempt.
inj_report.long: Johnston was targeted on just 9.5 percent of Justin Herbert's 21 pass attempts against New York. The wideout has now caught exactly one pass in three straight games and in five of his last six contests. Johnston is a lightly targeted deep threat who will likely continue to see fewer looks if Ladd McConkey is able to maintain his health for an extended period.

inj_report.short: Felton caught six of 12 targets for 42 yards during Sunday night's 35-10 loss to the 49ers.
inj_report.long: Felton was set to operate in an expanded role with Jordan Addison (thumb) on injured reserve, and he garnered a game-high 12 targets. The wide receiver finished tied for second on the team in catches with tight end T.J. Hockenson while fellow wideout Justin Jefferson (seven) led the way. Felton has caught nine of 17 targets for 75 yards over the last two weeks, and his next chance to build off of his recent momentum will come in Week 12 against the Falcons.

inj_report.short: Barner caught all three targets for 19 yards in Sunday's 21-13 win over the Raiders.
inj_report.long: Barner has been held below 25 receiving yards in eight of 10 games this season and has more rushing touchdowns (two) than receiving scores (one) during the 2026 campaign. He's the definition of a low-floor, touchdown-or-bust fantasy option headed into the team's bye week.

inj_report.short: Higgins caught his lone target for four yards during the Cardinals' 34-7 loss to the Chiefs on Sunday.
inj_report.long: The Cardinals offense struggled Sunday with Josh Johnson as the starter in the absence of Carson Beck (back). Of Johnson's 31 pass attempts, 26 of them were split between Trey McBride (14), Harrison Wallace (seven) and Simi Fehoko (five), leaving very little for Higgins and the other Cardinals pass catchers. Higgins has only one catch over his last two outings and a 19-166-1 line on 21 targets through 11 regular-season games.

inj_report.short: Parkinson caught both of his targets for 11 yards during the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
inj_report.long: Parkinson was able to shed an injury designation for Sunday's game after having his practice reps limited during Week 10 prep due to a lingering rib injury. His second catch of the contest went for 10 yards early in the third quarter and set the Rams up on the 1-yard line, with Blake Corum finding the end zone on the next play. Parkinson was on the field for 53 of the Rams' 76 offensive snaps (69.7 percent), and fellow tight ends Davis Allen (52) and Tyler Higbee (51) were not far behind. The Rams are committed to using their 13-man personnel, although the game plan could be slightly tweaked after the Week 11 bye if wide receiver Davante Adams (hamstring) is activated from injured reserve ahead of Week 12 against the Packers on Wednesday, Nov. 25. Parkinson has caught 20 passes (on 25 targets) for 127 yards and a touchdown through eight regular-season games.

inj_report.short: Monangai carried the ball eight times for 18 yards and failed to catch his only target in Sunday's 21-13 win over the Saints.
inj_report.long: Making his return from a five-game absence due to turf toe, Monangai wasn't able to generate much offense, as D'Andre Swift led the backfield with 15 touches and 59 scrimmage yards, plus a short receiving TD. Surprisingly, Salvon Ahmed also handled six carries, all in the fourth quarter when the game seemed well in hand. Monangai should see his usage increase as he puts the injury further behind him, and a late lost fumble by Swift -- his third of the season, a new career high -- might encourage coach Ben Johnson to prioritize Monangai even more in Week 12 against the Lions.

inj_report.short: Kiner carried the ball 10 times for 25 yards in Sunday's 35-10 loss to Detroit.
inj_report.long: Rhamondre Stevenson was active despite dealing with a knee issue during the practice week, but the veteran back gained just four yards on six carries, and Kiner wound up leading the Patriots' backfield in both volume and yardage. The entire offense struggles after Drake Maye (ankle) was knocked out of the game early, however. New England gets a Week 11 bye, so Kiner's role and usage for a Week 12 clash with the Chargers likely won't become clear until the health of Stevenson and Maye come into focus after the break.

inj_report.short: Taylor caught two passes for 25 yards on two targets in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Chargers.
inj_report.long: The Jets controlled this game from start to finish and never trailed, so Geno Smith attempted just 21 passes to 37 run plays for New York. Taylor's 25 yards were his most in a game since Week 7, and he's totaled just 10 catches for 75 yards and no touchdowns over his last four contests. He's a very risky play as a fantasy tight end.

Over his last six outings, Burks has caught 14 passes on 24 targets for 260 yards and two touchdowns, and he has operated as operated as the Commanders' WR3 since Terry McLaurin suffered a season-ending knee injury in Week 6 against the 49ers.

inj_report.short: Mayer posted one catch (on four targets) for four yards during Sunday's 38-24 defeat at Denver.
inj_report.long: Mayer missed out on a prime opportunity with top TE Brock Bowers (ankle/quadriceps) inactive in Week 11. When Bowers was out in Weeks 1 and 2 as he recovered from a meniscus trim in his left knee, Mayer went for a combined 9-55-0 line on 11 targets in those contests, but the latter also missed a stretch in the fourth quarter this Sunday due to a back injury. Bowers' status will be worth monitoring this week, as an absence from him next Sunday in Cleveland will set up Mayer for another key chance to produce.

inj_report.short: Croskey-Merritt rushed 13 times for 54 yards and a touchdown and brought in two of three targets for 23 yards in the Commanders' 22-20 win over the Bengals on Monday night.
inj_report.long: Making his return from a four-game absence due to a groin injury, Croskey-Merritt outpaced Austin Ekeler, the only other Commanders back to log a carry, by six rush attempts. The second-year pro also recorded his third rushing touchdown of the season on a one-yard run with 12 seconds remaining in the first half. Croskey-Merritt averaged over 4.0 yards per carry for the second straight game after failing to eclipse that mark in each of the first four games of the season, and he should be in store for an even busier day in a favorable Week 12 road matchup against the Cardinals on Sunday.

inj_report.short: Hill carried the ball six times for 69 yards and a touchdown and caught four of five targets for 27 yards in Sunday's 35-33 loss to the Panthers.
inj_report.long: Derrick Henry had a strong performance as well but was knocked out of the game in the fourth quarter and got checked for a concussion. Hill was heavily involved in the offense prior to that, however, scoring from 19 yards out in the late in the second quarter. He almost had a second TD earlier in the quarter, but Hill had the ball punched loose at the one-yard line after a 36-yard scamper and saw it bounce out of the end zone for a turnover and a touchback. Henry cleared the concussion protocol after the game and figures to be active in the Week 12 against the Texans, but Hill's usage appears to be on the upswing as the Ravens' No. 2 back.

inj_report.short: Price posted nine carries for 36 yards and one touchdown and gathered in his only target for eight yards during Sunday's 21-13 victory at Las Vegas.
inj_report.long: This marks Price's fewest touches in a game since returning from IR in Week 8, and he actually was doubled up in the category by position mate Zach Charbonnet, who turned his 20 rushes into 94 yards. Having said that, Price salvaged his day with a 12-yard TD, the first of his career, on the ground in the third quarter. The breakdown of work between the two may signal what's to come in the Seahawks backfield after the team's Week 11 bye, with Price and company set to face off with the NFC West-leading 49ers on the road on Sunday, Nov. 29.

Dell has played an effective complementary role since making his return from a gruesome 2024 knee injury in Week 7, as he now has an 11-196-1 line and four catches of 20-plus yards across 18 targets heading into a Week 12 home matchup against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 29.

inj_report.short: Dotson caught three passes for 63 yards on six targets in Sunday's 35-13 loss to the Chiefs.
inj_report.long: Dotson has yet to hit 100 receiving yards in a game this season and has just two touchdowns, but he leads the league averaging 21.9 yards per catch, turning his 19 grabs into 416 yards through 10 games. He's fighting for leftover opportunities behind Drake London, Bijan Robinson and Kyle Pitts in Atlanta's offense. Dotson isn't a reliable fantasy option down the stretch and headed into the Falcons' Week 11 bye.

inj_report.short: Johnson rushed 23 times for 105 yards and a touchdown and brought in all four targets for 38 yards in the Chiefs' 34-7 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
inj_report.long: Making a second consecutive start in place of Kenneth Walker (groin), Johnson once again provided starter-quality production as both a runner and receiver. The rookie also added his second career rushing TD on a three-yard run late in the first quarter, making it an all-around rewarding fantasy day. The Chiefs expect Walker to be ready to return for a Thanksgiving night showdown against the Bills in four days, but even if that comes to pass, Johnson has likely earned himself a larger role for the stretch run with his performance the last two contests.

inj_report.short: Lane didn't garner a target during Sunday's 35-33 loss to the Panthers.
inj_report.long: Lane failed to reel in a pass for the second time in three weeks, and both times the ball was thrown his way Sunday, the play was negated by a defensive penalty, resulting in no targets for the rookie. Lane was on the field for 33 offensive snaps, ranking third at wide receiver for Baltimore behind Rashod Bateman (59) and Zay Flowers (57). Lane's next chance to get back on track will come in Week 12 against the Texans.

inj_report.short: Washington caught all three targets for 22 yards in Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Eagles.
inj_report.long: The big tight end earned just a 6.8 percent target share on a day when Aaron Rodgers fired off 44 pass attempts in prolonged comeback mode. Washington has been held to 25 yards or fewer in eight of 10 games this season. He doesn't see enough volume to warrant weekly fantasy consideration as a touchdown-or-bust bet.

inj_report.short: Vidal carried the ball seven times for 36 yards and caught both his targets for 18 yards in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Jets.
inj_report.long: After handling just four touches last week against the Ravens, Vidal saw his usage increase again as he recorded his most scrimmage yards since Week 5. This time, however, his additional volume came at the expense of Keaton Mitchell (knee), who left the game early. Omarion Hampton has re-established himself as the Chargers' clear No. 1 RB over the last few contests, but if Mitchell's injury proves to be serious, Vidal could have some deeper-league appeal with the No. 2 role all to himself. He'll look to take advantage of whatever opportunities he gets in Week 12 against the Patriots.

inj_report.short: Allen totaled three catches (on four targets) for 38 yards during Sunday's 35-10 victory against the Vikings in Mexico City.
inj_report.long: Sunday marked Allen's first time working with Mike Evans, the 49ers' top wide receiver, and the latter dominated the attention of QB Brock Purdy, posting a 6-109-1 line on seven targets in his first game action since Week 6. If Evans' Achilles issue flares up at any point, Allen may be thrust into WR1 duties, which could yield more consistent results as he becomes more acclimated to head coach Kyle Shanahan's offense. For now, though, Allen will play a distant second to Evans for as long as the latter is healthy and available.

inj_report.short: Lloyd finished Sunday's loss to Minnesota with 13 yards on four carries while catching all three of his targets for 26 yards.
inj_report.long: With Josh Jacobs (finger) sidelined, Green Bay turned to the trio of Lloyd, Kaleb Johnson and Chris Brooks in the backfield. Johnson led the team with 10 carries and 42 total yards despite not getting any targets. Meanwhile, Lloyd turned his seven touches into 39 yards, and Brooks tallied just three yards on his three touches. Green Bay is on bye during the coming week, but Jacobs may still miss the team's next game, which will take place Wednesday, Nov. 25, against the Rams. If that's the case, Lloyd will likely work as part of a shared backfield again, which isn't great for his fantasy outlook.

inj_report.long: The Saints expect to have a better feel for Johnson's status Wednesday, when the team holds its first practice of Week 12. Before exiting Sunday in the third quarter, Johnson was targeted just once and failed to record a reception for the second time in 10 appearances on the season. If the hamstring injury prevents Johnson from playing next weekend in Cincinnati, Noah Fant and Oscar Delp would be in line for added snaps at tight end.

inj_report.short: Johnson handled the first RB reps during the open portion of Sunday's practice, Mike Spofford of the Packers' official site reports.
inj_report.long: Josh Jacobs logged his first official practice Sunday since undergoing finger surgery on Nov. 13, going down as a limited participant. Head coach Matt LaFleur relayed to Wes Hodkiewicz of the team's official site earlier in the day that Jacobs is "gonna have to show a lot of progress" the next few days to be available in Week 12. If Jacobs isn't active Wednesday at the Rams, Johnson may be the favorite to lead Green Bay's backfield in carries and rushing yards, as he did in a Week 10 loss to the Vikings, when he took 10 rushes for 42 yards. Meanwhile, fellow RB MarShawn Lloyd had seven touches for 39 yards from scrimmage in that contest, and Chris Brooks logged three touches for three total yards.

inj_report.long: The tight end earned just a 9.1 percent target share and continues to be nearly invisible in the box score despite being an every-down player who runs virtually every pass route for the Bucs. Otton has just one touchdown since Week 11 of the 2024 season and has just one career 100-yard receiving game across 73 regular-season contests. He's a touchdown-or-bust fantasy bet who clearly busts far more than he hits.

inj_report.short: Gainwell rushed four times for 16 yards and brought in four of five targets for 43 yards in the Buccaneers 31-21 loss to the Lions on Sunday.
inj_report.long: Gainwell held his usual complementary role on the ground behind a busy Bucky Irving, yet with the Buccaneers trailing throughout the second half, Gainwell was able to finish second in receptions, receiving yards and targets on the day for Tampa Bay. The veteran back has back-to-back 16-yard efforts on the ground, but Gainwell has a combined 7-103-0 line through the air in that same span heading into a Week 12 home matchup against the Panthers on Monday night, Nov. 30.

It was notable that Jordyn Tyson ran just 22 routes on Tyler Shough's 51 dropbacks against Chicago. The Saints offense has become tough to predict on a week-to-week basis. And Jeanty was the engine of the Raiders offense Sunday, racking up 16 touches for 169 yards from scrimmage and one receiving TD. A rookie fourth-rounder, Washington is averaging just 3.9 yards per carry and has scored only one touchdown ahead of next Sunday's road matchup with the Browns.

inj_report.short: Kupp hauled in his lone target for a 34-yard touchdown during the Seahawks' 21-13 win over the Raiders on Sunday.
inj_report.long: It was the third time this season that Kupp recorded only one catch, but the veteran wide receiver made his lone reception count when he found open space on a broken play to connect with Drew Lock for a TD late in the first quarter. It was the third touchdown catch of the season for Kupp, two of which have come over his last three outings. He'll enter the bye with a 23-272-3 line on 35 targets through 10 regular-season games, and the Seahawks' next matchup will take place in Week 12 on the road against the 49ers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

inj_report.short: Worthy caught two of four targets for 38 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 34-7 win over the Cardinals.
inj_report.long: Worthy was able to eclipse 30 receiving yards for just the second time in the last five weeks, but it was a step in the right direction after being blanked on three targets in Week 10. The wide receiver's biggest moment of the game came in the fourth quarter when he connected with quarterback Patrick Mahomes for an 18-yard touchdown. The score was Worthy's second of the year and first since Week 2, and his next chance to build off of Sunday's performance will come on Thanksgiving against the Bills.

inj_report.long: The veteran running back played just eight of 72 offensive snaps, while both CJ Donaldson and Travis Etienne played 32 each with Audric Estime a healthy inactive. Kamara has touched the ball just seven times on 24 snaps over the past two weeks, but he's turned three of those touches into short touchdowns. Kamara's proverbial gas tank is nearing empty, but the Saints continue to give him high-value touches near the goal line while refusing to play him outside of the red zone.

Raridon also has been held to single-digit receiving yards in two of the last three contests. He's averaging a robust 13.6 yards per catch this season but isn't a reliable fantasy option with Hunter Henry healthy.

inj_report.long: The wideout led his position group by playing 52 of 56 offensive snaps, and he ran a team-high 34 routes on Josh Johnson's 37 dropbacks. It didn't translate to much production outside of the short touchdown, as Fehoko has consistently shown he can't win enough as an NFL receiver. He's been thrust into heavy snaps due to a litany of injuries in Arizona. Fehoko can mostly be ignored in fantasy until he shows something more in the box score.

inj_report.short: Helm caught two of three targets for 14 yards in Sunday's 51-30 loss to the Cowboys.
inj_report.long: The tight end has yet to catch a touchdown this season and was unable to get anything going against arguably the league's worst defense Sunday. Helm has been held below 30 receiving yards in nine of 10 games this season. He's nothing more than a low-end TE2 in fantasy.

inj_report.short: Harris caught both his targets for 28 yards in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Jets.
inj_report.long: With Ladd McConkey back in the lineup, Harris' role in the passing attack shrank after he'd turned 12 targets over the prior two games into an 8-92-0 line. Harris' fantasy appeal would collapse even further if Justin Herbert (concussion) ends up missing any time. The second-year wideout will at least get a promising matchup in Week 12 against a vulnerable Patriots secondary.

inj_report.long: It was Brooks' first action since Week 4 after spending five games on injured reserve with a high-ankle sprain. With Josh Jacobs (finger) inactive against Minnesota, Brooks led the backfield with 26 offensive snaps in Week 10, but it didn't translate to touches or opportunities to handle the football. With Kaleb Johnson and MarShawn Lloyd also involved, it's difficult to pinpoint any of these three as reliable fantasy options despite Jacobs' absence.

inj_report.short: Vaki took one carry for a loss of one yard and caught his only target for seven yards during Sunday's 31-21 win versus the Buccaneers.
inj_report.long: Of the Lions' 58 offensive snaps in Week 11, Vaki played just 13, his lowest count since back in Week 7 versus the Packers (9). Starter Jahmyr Gibbs compiled 100-plus scrimmage yards and multiple scrimmage touchdowns for the fifth time in 10 games Sunday, so should continue to get all the work he can handle in a Thanksgiving matchup versus the Bears, leaving only whatever is left behind to Vaki.

Atwell played behind both Konata Mumpfield and CJ Daniels at receiver for Los Angeles.

inj_report.short: Dobbins logged just one snap in Sunday's 38-24 win over the Raiders, though head coach Sean Payton said Monday that Dobbins "is going to be super important" moving forward, Will Petersen of 104.3 The Fan reports.
inj_report.long: Dobbins' opportunities have been dwindling since Week 7 against Arizona, when he dropped to 14 offensive snaps after tallying 31 the week prior. That contest against the Cardinals was when rookie Jonah Coleman returned from a four-game absence, and Coleman has since forced his way into Denver's lead-RB role with blossoming production that has included five rushing TDs over his past three games. Coleman got nearly every running-back snap for Denver on Sunday, with practice-squad elevation Cody Schrader logging just two snaps and Dobbins one. Despite Payton's proclamation that Dobbins still has a "super important" role with the team, there's little reason to expect him to be a reliable fantasy asset as long as Coleman is healthy.

inj_report.short: Ekeler rushed nine times for 26 yards and brought in all four targets for 26 yards in the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday.
inj_report.long: As his final line indicates, Ekeler retained a solid level of involvement in the narrow win, logging a season-high 13 touches. He posted a new season high in receiving yards along the way, and the veteran back has proven to be a solid complement to Rachaad White while Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin, IR) has been sidelined. However, with the latter potentially set to return as soon as Week 11's home matchup against the Bengals, Ekeler could be headed to a reduced role.

inj_report.short: Thomas caught one pass for an 18-yard touchdown on three targets in Sunday's 23-18 loss to the Giants.
inj_report.long: Thomas' three targets were a distant fourth on the team, as Parker Washington (17), Jakobi Meyers (10) and Josh Cameron (seven) combined to see a combined 34 looks on Trevor Lawrence's 47 pass attempts. Thomas ran 32 routes, 14 more than Cameron as the Jaguars' nominal WR3, but the former hasn't been seeing meaningful target volume for months. After drawing nine targets in Week 2, Thomas has averaged 2.1 targets per game over his last eight contests. He's well off the fantasy radar while Washington and Meyers are healthy.

inj_report.short: Herbert caught two of his three targets for seven yards during Sunday's 35-13 loss versus the Chiefs. He also returned six kickoffs for 168 yards.
inj_report.long: Herbert was targeted three times for the second straight game in Week 10, but he continued to make a bigger impact on special teams. His first kickoff return of the day went for 39 yards to Atlanta's 45-yard line, but the offense promptly went three and out. He'll be hoping to keep up the momentum as a returner following the Falcons' bye in Week 11.

inj_report.short: Sample caught all three of his targets for 15 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 38-18 win against Pittsburgh.
inj_report.long: Sample entered the contest with no catches over his previous two games, but he tied season-high marks in both receptions and targets versus the Steelers. He gave Cincinnati a two-score lead just after the beginning of the second quarter when he hauled in a three-yard TD from Joe Burrow. Sample has two touchdowns over his past four games, but with just five catches for 39 yards during that span, he's almost entirely dependent on getting into the end zone to generate useful fantasy production.

inj_report.short: Bell caught one of his four targets for eight yards in the Dolphins' 26-9 loss to the Bills on Sunday.
inj_report.long: Bell saw 34 offensive snaps in Sunday's contest. The wide receiver played in 62 percent of the Dolphins' offensive plays but only caught one pass. The team continues to try to involve the third-round rookie, but for one reason or another, he remains out of sync with quarterbacks Malik Willis (abdomen) and Kyle McCord.

inj_report.short: Black notched six carries for eight yards and secured his only target for seven yards during Sunday's 35-10 win versus the Vikings in Mexico City.
inj_report.long: Black entered Week 11 action on the heels of three consecutive contests with double-digit touches, so Sunday's performance was a step back to his modest outings from Weeks 2-6. In any case, the rookie third-round pick continues to be utilized regularly in the 49ers offense, averaging 9.1 touches for 37.8 yards from scrimmage per game while working as the clear No. 2 RB behind Christian McCaffrey. Black's next chance to contribute arrives next Sunday against the Seahawks.

inj_report.short: Cameron caught three of seven targets for 44 yards during Sunday's 23-18 loss against the Giants. He also returned two kickoffs for a total of 40 return yards.
inj_report.long: Despite only being on the field for 25 of the Jaguars' 68 offensive snaps in Week 11, Cameron drew a career-high seven targets. He wasn't terribly efficient on those targets, but neither was Jacksonville's offense as a whole Sunday. He'll be lining up against a much softer pass defense in a Week 12 tilt versus the Titans.

inj_report.short: TeSlaa failed to catch any of his three targets during Sunday's 31-21 win over the Buccaneers.
inj_report.long: TeSlaa went without a reception for the second time in four weeks, and he has now gone six straight games without exceeding 20 receiving yards. The wide receiver played 23 snaps on offense, ranking third at his position behind Amon-Ra St. Brown (46) and Jameson Williams (45). TeSlaa will continue to be an unreliable fantasy option ahead of the team's Week 12 matchup with the Bears on Thursday.

inj_report.short: Njoku caught two of four passes for 28 yards during the Chargers' 27-24 loss to the Jets on Sunday.
inj_report.long: Njoku briefly left Sunday's contest after injuring his shoulder at the end of a 13-yard catch in the first quarter. The veteran tight end was cleared to return, and he ended up finishing second on the Chargers in targets behind Ladd McConkey (eight) on a day in which Justin Herbert completed 15 of 21 passes for 131 yards and two touchdowns. Njoku and the Chargers stay home for Week 12 against the Patriots on Nov. 29.

inj_report.short: Hollins caught five of six targets for 48 yards in Sunday's 35-10 loss to the Lions in Munich.
inj_report.long: In his second game back from a calf injury, Hollins led the Patriots in catches and receiving yards, but the entire offense was compromised when Drake Maye (ankle) was knocked out of the game early. A.J. Brown (hamstring) also didn't last long in his latest return to action. New England gets a bye in Week 11, giving the team's injured stars a chance to recover, so Hollins' role and usage may not become clear until after the break. Over six appearances this season, Hollins has produced a 23-293-1 line on 32 targets.

inj_report.short: Jeudy recorded two catches on four targets for 74 yards in a 27-24 victory over the Texans on Sunday.
inj_report.long: Jeudy boosted his final line considerably on a 65-yard connection with Deshaun Watson in the second period. Watson carried the ball into the end zone on the following snap to bring the Browns to within seven points. Jeudy's 74 receiving yards were a season-high mark, though he finished with two or fewer receptions for the third straight week. The veteran wideout is behind both WRs Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion, not to mention tight end Harold Fannin, in the pass-catcher pecking order, so he may need to rely on big plays to have a chance to make an impact for fantasy managers.

inj_report.short: Williams caught two passes for 27 yards on two targets in Sunday's 30-10 loss to the Vikings.
inj_report.long: As he's been doing since making his season debut in Week 6, Williams operated as the Packers' third receiver against Minnesota. He logged 20 offensive snaps and ran 16 routes on 37 dropbacks. Williams has yet to hit 50 receiving yards in any of his five games this season and has no real fantasy appeal in 12-team fantasy leagues. He's well behind Matthew Golden, Christian Watson and Tucker Kraft in the order for touches and targets.

inj_report.short: Mims caught one of two targets for 36 yards and also added an 11-yard rush and 22 yards as a punt returner during Sunday's 38-24 win over the Raiders.
inj_report.long: Mims reeled in just one pass for the second straight game, but his 36-yard snag in the second quarter was enough to notch his second highest receiving yardage total in a contest this year. The wideout played just 15 snaps on offense, which ranked fifth at his position behind Courtland Sutton (49), Pat Bryant (40), Jaylen Waddle (39) and Troy Franklin (24) for Denver in Week 11. Mims will remain an unappealing fantasy option ahead of Friday's matchup with the Steelers.

inj_report.short: Kolar brought in his lone target for eight yards during the Chargers' 27-24 loss to the Jets on Sunday.
inj_report.long: Kolar was cleared to play Sunday after progressing through the league's concussion protocol, and his 30 offensive snaps were ahead of fellow tight ends David Njoku (25) and Oronde Gadsden (23). Kolar's eight-yard catch midway through the first quarter was the only pass that the fifth-year pro saw from Justin Herbert, but no Chargers pass catcher saw more than five targets other then Ladd McConkey (eight). Kolar has a 16-153-0 line on 24 targets through eight regular-season games heading into Week 12 against the Patriots on Nov. 29.

inj_report.short: Burks was targeted three times for zero catches, had one kick return for 10 yards and made one tackle on kick coverage during the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday night.
inj_report.long: Burks was the No. 2 wide receiver for the Colts in the contest. Despite being targeted three times, the wide receiver could not haul in any passes from since-cut quarterback Daniel Jones. Burks played 32 offensive snaps and two special-teams snaps in the contest.

inj_report.short: Gray (ribs) was deemed a non-participant in Monday's walkthrough.
inj_report.long: Kansas City didn't actually practice Monday, but Gray's DNP tag is nonetheless concerning with the club set to take the field Thursday versus Buffalo. Gray was injured late in Sunday's win over Arizona and didn't re-enter the contest. If the veteran tight end isn't able to suit up against the Bills, Jake Briningstool could see more work on offense as Travis Kelce's backup.

inj_report.short: Allen caught his lone target for a 19-yard touchdown in Sunday's win over the Cardinals.
inj_report.long: With all three of Puka Nacua (knee/toe), Davante Adams (hamstring) and Terrance Ferguson (hamstring) out, the Rams leaned on their tight-end triumvirate of Tyler Higbee, Colby Parkinson and Allen, as all three played more offensive snaps than any of the Los Angeles wideouts. Parkinson (53 snaps) led the way, followed by Allen (52) and Higbee (51), and both Allen and Higbee caught touchdowns. Allen, however, ran just six routes on Matthew Stafford's 28 dropbacks, so it's not enough to warrant consideration in fantasy leagues.

inj_report.short: Donaldson logged a five-yard carry and brought in all four of his targets for 12 yards during the Saints' 21-13 loss to the Bears on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.
inj_report.long: Donaldson recorded season highs in both catches and targets, and he finished third on the Saints in both of those categories behind Chris Olave and Devaughn Vele. However, Donaldson coughed up the football on his first catch of the game early in the second quarter, which the Bears offense capitalized on with a six-play drive that ended with a three-yard touchdown pass from Caleb Williams to D'Andre Swift. Donaldson's 32 offensive snaps were tied with Travis Etienne for most among Saints running backs Sunday, although Etienne saw a heavier workload with 14 carries for 76 yards while Alvin Kamara, who played only eight offensive snaps, found the end zone on a one-yard touchdown pass from Tyler Shough in the second quarter. Losers of three of their last four games, the Saints will look to reverse their fortunes in Week 12 against the Bengals on Nov. 29.

inj_report.short: Thomas brought in two of three targets for 56 yards and added a 30-yard carry during the Bears' 21-13 win over the Saints on Sunday.
inj_report.long: Thomas was cleared to play Sunday after working through an ankle issue that prevented him from practicing Friday. The ankle didn't appear to bother him, as he turned his first touch of the game into a 30-yard rush midway through the second quarter before connecting with Caleb Williams for 40 and 16 yards in the third and fourth quarters, respectively. It was the rookie third-round wideout's best performance of the season, and while Chicago boasts talented pass catchers like Luther Burden, Rome Odunze and Colston Loveland, Thomas' big-play potential could be something that the Bears lean into for Thanksgiving Day against the Lions, whose defense ranks 27th in the NFL in passing yards allowed per game (233.1) and 29th in passing touchdowns allowed (21).

inj_report.short: Chism did not catch his only target during the Patriots' 35-10 loss against the Lions in Munich in Week 10.
inj_report.long: A.J. Brown (hamstring) returned from a two-game absence caused by ankle and knee injuries in Week 10, and as a result, Chism saw his lowest snap count this season (8) since he was a healthy scratch in Week 1. His role coming out of the Patriots' bye in Week 11 will probably depend heavily on the availability of Brown, who picked up a hamstring issue against the Lions.

inj_report.short: Bech caught eight of nine targets for 88 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 38-24 loss to the Broncos.
inj_report.long: Bech finished second on the team in targets behind fellow wideout Tre Tucker (10), and he was able to reel in a seven-yard touchdown pass from quarterback Fernando Mendoza in the fourth quarter. The score was Bech's first since Week 1, and his 88 receiving yards bested his previous season total of 67 yards entering Week 11. The wide receiver appears to have great chemistry with Mendoza, garnering 16 targets over the quarterback's first two career starts.

inj_report.short: Evans caught all five of his targets for 44 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 35-33 win over the Ravens.
inj_report.long: Evans was able to reel in a season-high five passes while notching multiple receptions for the fourth time in five weeks. The tight end's biggest moment of the game came in the first quarter when he secured a 23-yard touchdown pass from quarterback Bryce Young, registering his first score of the year. Evans has now caught 17 of 20 targets for 191 yards and a touchdown over 10 contests during the 2026 campaign.

inj_report.short: Knox caught two of three targets for 31 yards in Sunday's 26-9 win over the Dolphins.
inj_report.long: Knox was the top available TE for the Bills in the absence of Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle). The added opportunities helped Knox post his second-highest total of the season in receiving yards, but Knox remains off the radar in most fantasy formats heading into Thursday's game against the Chiefs. He hasn't scored since Week 2 while recording a meager 117 yards on 16 catches through 10 games.

inj_report.short: Ridley caught five of six targets for 68 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 51-30 loss to the Cowboys.
inj_report.long: Ridley reeled in multiple passes in a contest for the first time since Week 5, and his 12-yard touchdown connection with Cam Ward in the fourth quarter was the wideout's first score of the year. Ridley trailed only fellow wide receiver Chimere Dike (seven) in targets, and Ridley could continue to see added opportunities moving forward with Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) sidelined for the remainder of the 2026 campaign.

inj_report.short: Giddens will likely move up to the No. 2 RB role for the Colts in the short term, as Seth McGowan is expected to miss time due to a hamstring injury, James Boyd of The Athletic reports.
inj_report.long: Head coach Shane Steichen said Monday that McGowan "will miss some time" but didn't specify how long the absence may be. For however long McGowan is sidelined, Giddens figures to serve as Jonathan Taylor's backup at running back. Giddens has shown some flashes this season in limited playing time, amassing 48 yards on seven carries (6.9 YPC) and catching his only target for 11 yards over three games.

inj_report.short: Johnson caught his only target for 15 yards during Sunday's 23-18 win versus the Jaguars.
inj_report.long: Johnson was third in offensive snaps among Giants tight ends Sunday (14) behind starter Isaiah Likely (49) and veteran Chris Manhertz (19). With that said, Johnson did manage to record at least one catch for the fourth time in his last five games. As long as Likely remains available, though, Johnson will probably remain in a rotational role.

inj_report.long: The rookie third-rounder connected with Caleb Williams for a 19-yard catch midway through the first quarter, although Roush didn't see another target the rest of the way. With Cole Kmet (knee, IR) out for the rest of the year, Roush will continue to serve as the Bears' TE2 behind Colston Loveland. The Bears are on the road for Thanksgiving Day against the Lions, whose defense ranks dead last in the NFL in fantasy points allowed per game to opposing tight ends.

inj_report.short: Nailor caught one of five targets for 16 yards during Sunday's 38-24 loss to the Broncos.
inj_report.long: Nailor caught one pass for the second straight week, and he has exceeded 20 receiving yards only one time since Week 1. The wide receiver was unable to capitalize on the absence of Brock Bowers (ankle) in Week 11, and Nailor figures to remain an unattractive fantasy option in Week 12 against the Browns.

inj_report.long: Cooper played 46 offensive snaps and 15 special-teams snaps in Sunday's contest. The wide receiver continues to play most of the offensive snaps for the Eagles, seeing two more targets than rookie first-round pick Makai Lemon in the Week 11 win.

inj_report.short: Williams failed to haul in his lone target during the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions on Sunday in Munich.
inj_report.long: Williams did have a 21-yard carry late in the third quarter, although the play was nullified by offsetting penalties. It was the second straight game that the second-year wide receiver did not record a catch and the fifth time in 10 regular-season contests. New England is on a bye for Week 11, but the offense's outlook looks grim given that franchise quarterback Drake Maye is expected to miss time due to an ankle injury that he sustained in the first quarter of Sunday's game. The Patriots' next game takes place in Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

inj_report.long: Dallas Goedert (47 snaps), Johnny Mundt (eight) and Zach Ertz (six) handled tight-end duties for Philly, while Stowers played 20 snaps on special teams. The rookie tight end is miles from fantasy relevance this season.

Price continues to show out on special teams, with 912 kick return yards and 281 punt return yards over 10 games so far in 2026.

inj_report.short: Trautman caught his only target for a one-yard touchdown during Sunday's 38-24 win versus the Raiders.
inj_report.long: Trautman leaked open behind Las Vegas' defense on a play-action pass from the goal line early in the second quarter, giving Denver a 10-0 lead. He still has a big role in the Broncos' offense, but he isn't running enough routes to sustain pass-catching production worth fantasy consideration in most formats.

inj_report.short: Restrepo caught his lone target for five yards in Sunday's 51-30 loss to the Cowboys.
inj_report.long: Even with Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) out, Restrepo played as the Titans' WR5 against Dallas, as his 17 offensive snaps trailed all four of Carnell Tate (61), Chimere Dike (53), Elic Ayomanor (36) and Calvin Ridley (26) in terms of playing time. Restrepo played 11 of his 13 snaps on pass plays in the slot, where Robinson operated prior to his injury, but it was actually Dike and Daniel Bellinger who saw the biggest boosts in slot rate with Robinson out.

inj_report.short: Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer confirmed Tuesday that Corbin will be elevated from the practice squad for Thursday's game against the Eagles, Nick Harris of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram reports.
inj_report.long: Corbin will be back up with the Cowboys for the second time in as many weeks after making a positive impression in his team debut during this past Sunday's 51-30 win over the Titans. He served as the top backup to starting running back Javonte Williams in that contest, finishing with five carries for 32 yards and one catch for five yards while logging 18 of the Cowboys' 65 offensive snaps. Another strong showing in Week 12 could give Corbin a shot at earning a permanent spot on the 53-man roster.

inj_report.short: Walker recorded 211 kickoff-return yards, including an 86-yard touchdown, and one catch for 34 yards in Sunday's 35-33 loss to the Panthers.
inj_report.long: The wide receiver took on the role for the first time this season and did well. Walker has seen just 10 targets on offense in 2026, so he's not much of a factor in fantasy leagues at the moment, but he can perhaps find his place on the return team.

Baltimore will take on the Texans in Week 12.

inj_report.long: Wright continues to struggle rushing the ball this season, averaging just 1.6 yards per carry across 30 rush attempts. The 23-year-old will look to improve upon his performance during the Week 12 matchup versus the Jets.

inj_report.short: Horton failed to garner a target during Sunday's 21-13 win over the Raiders.
inj_report.long: Horton failed to reel in a pass for the first time since Week 7, and his 10 offensive snaps ranked fourth at wide receiver for Seattle behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba (43), Cooper Kupp (35) and Rashid Shaheed (25). Horton will continue to be an unappealing fantasy option as long as he's buried below the other three wideouts on the depth chart.

inj_report.short: Meyers caught both of his targets for 20 yards and a touchdown while also adding 58 yards as a kick returner during Sunday night's 38-18 win over the Steelers.
inj_report.long: Meyers reeled in multiple passes for the third straight game, and he was able to secure his first score of the year in the second quarter on a 15-yard touchdown pass from Joe Burrow. The 26-year-old's 28 offensive snaps ranked fourth at wide receiver for Cincinnati behind Ja'Marr Chase (59), Tee Higgins (51) and Colbie Young (29). With Andrei Iosivas (thumb) nearing a return to action, Meyers may see a sharp drop in offensive opportunities in the near future.

inj_report.short: Moreau brought in his lone target for eight yards during the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts on Thursday.
inj_report.long: Moreau's 30 offensive snaps were second among Texans tight ends behind Dalton Schultz's 34, yet it was Marlin Klein who led the position group with four catches (on as many targets) for 24 yards, including a 13-yard touchdown pass from C.J. Stroud late in the third quarter. Moreau is up to a 12-80-3 receiving line on 15 targets through 10 regular-season games and has caught one pass or zero in five of those contests. He doesn't have much fantasy appeal unless Schultz were to miss time.

inj_report.short: Franklin did not record a catch in Sunday's 38-24 win over the Raiders.
inj_report.long: The wide receiver did see two targets, but he wasn't able to haul them in. Franklin has just 17 targets across 10 games this year, making nine catches for 100 yards and no scores.

inj_report.short: Carter reverted to the Titans' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
inj_report.long: With Tyjae Spears (knee) back on the shelf and sent to injured reserve over the weekend, Carter played 14 of 68 offensive snaps behind Tony Pollard in Sunday's 51-30 loss to the Cowboys. Carter ended up carrying the ball four times for nine yards and caught is lone target for two yards. He should remain Pollard's backup for at least the next three games while Spears is out unless the Titans have a change of heart and want to start getting rookie Nicholas Singleton some playing time.

inj_report.short: Turpin failed to reel in his only target while rushing twice for 41 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 51-30 win over the Titans. He added 121 yards as a kick returner and logged a 13-yard punt return.
inj_report.long: Turpin went without a catch for the fourth time this season, but he was able to make his mark as a rusher in Week 11. The wideout was able to break loose for a 22-yard rushing touchdown in the first quarter, notching his second score on the ground this season. Turpin has now caught five of 11 targets for 49 yards, rushed five times for 60 yards and two touchdowns, and added 695 kick-return yards and 121 yards as a punt returner over eight contests so far during the 2026 season.

inj_report.long: With Chris Bell (knee) back from his absence, Coleman reverted to WR4 duties for Miami, playing just 12 of 57 offensive snaps. He has no fantasy appeal while Caleb Douglas, Malik Washington and Bell are healthy. Coleman has been extremely inefficient through 10 games this season, catching just nine of 28 targets for 88 yards and two touchdowns.

inj_report.short: Legette did not play an offensive snap in Sunday's 35-33 win over the Ravens.
inj_report.long: The wide receiver did play nine snaps on special teams. Legette missed six games with a knee injury before returning for Carolina's win over the Saints in Week 10, though he only saw action on two offensive snaps in that contest. Legette has two catches for 64 yards and no touchdowns in four games this season.

inj_report.short: Larison turned his lone carry into two yards and caught two of three targets for 15 yards and a touchdown during the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions on Sunday in Munich. He also recorded a tackle on special teams.
inj_report.long: The Patriots lost starting quarterback Drake Maye to an ankle injury early in the first quarter, so backup Tommy DeVito was under center for most of contest. New England struggled with DeVito at the helm, but he did connect with Larison for a 10-yard touchdown pass early in the fourth quarter in what was the Patriots' lone trip to the end zone. Even though that score came in garbage time, it was the first touchdown of Larison's NFL career, although he's firmly entrenched as the team's RB3 behind Rhamondre Stevenson and Corey Kiner. The Patriots are on a bye for Week 11, so their next game will take place in Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

inj_report.short: Hurst caught five of seven targets for 56 yards and two touchdowns during Sunday's 31-21 loss to the Lions.
inj_report.long: Hurst led the team in targets, and his five catches and 56 receiving yards were new season highs. The wide receiver was able to reach paydirt twice, reeling in a 23-yard touchdown pass from quarterback Baker Mayfield in the second quarter before the pair connected for a four-yard score in the fourth quarter. Hurst has now caught 16 of 32 targets for 224 yards and three touchdowns over 10 contests this season.

inj_report.short: Delp hauled in his lone target for a six-yard reception in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Bears.
inj_report.long: The rookie third-round pick out of Georgia has handled a muted role at tight end behind Juwan Johnson and Noah Fant this season, compiling five receptions for 26 yards on five targets through nine appearances. Delp was limited to just 21 of the Saints' 72 offensive snaps in Week 11, but he could see his playing time pick up if the hamstring injury that knocked Johnson out of Sunday's loss early prevents him from suiting up this coming weekend in Cincinnati.

inj_report.short: Jones reverted to the Cardinals' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
inj_report.long: Jones' 32 snaps on offense during Sunday's 34-7 loss to the Chiefs were ahead of both Devin Duvernay and Reggie Virgil (two each) and behind Simi Fehoko (52) and Harrison Wallace (36). Jones finished the game with a one-yard carry and a 17-yard catch on two targets, and that reception ended up being the second-longest offensive play for the Cardinals. Given his usage in Week 11, Jones stands a good chance of being brought up for Week 12 against the Commanders on Nov. 29, although his next elevation from the practice squad is the last one he is eligible for this season.

inj_report.short: Wallace finished Sunday's loss to Kansas City with four catches for 57 yards on seven targets.
inj_report.long: Wallace began the season on the Cardinals' practice squad and didn't play in his first NFL game until Week 9 versus Seattle. After logging a total of seven offensive snaps and one catch across his first two contests, the rookie paced Arizona wideouts in targets, receptions and receiving yards. Wallace also ranked second among the wideout corps with 36 offensive snaps, so it appears there was a conscious effort to involve him in the team's passing game. The Cardinals' wide-receiver room has lacked a reliable option since Michael Wilson went down with a season-ending neck injury, so the door is wide open for Wallace to claim a prominent role with continued production.

inj_report.short: Bartholomew caught one of three targets for five yards in Sunday night's 35-10 loss to the 49ers.
inj_report.long: With T.J. Hockenson back in the lineup after being inactive Week 10, Bartholomew played just 18 of 67 offensive snaps as the Vikings' third tight end, also behind Ben Yurosek. Bartholomew has 11 catches for 95 yards and a touchdown on 15 targets across 10 games this season.

inj_report.short: Bellinger made one catch for five yards in the Titans' 51-30 loss to the Cowboys on Sunday.
inj_report.long: Bellinger played 26 offensive snaps and five special-teams snaps in the contest. The tight end made the most of his singular target but was primarily utilized as a blocker in the blowout loss.

inj_report.short: Wright caught both of two targets for 42 yards during Sunday's 31-21 win versus the Buccaneers.
inj_report.long: One of Wright's two grabs in Week 11 was a 27-yard strike up the seam, easily his longest reception of the season thus far. He was on the field for 43 of the Lions' 58 offensive snaps Sunday, but he spent a substantial majority of those on blocking assignments for tailback Jahmyr Gibbs and company. His role in a Thanksgiving tilt versus the Bears may depend somewhat on the health of running mate Sam Laporta, who was limited during Monday's walkthrough with an ankle issue.

inj_report.short: Shavers was targeted twice for zero catches and logged one tackle on kick coverage in the Bills' 26-9 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.
inj_report.long: Shavers played 27 offensive snaps and 16 special-teams in his return to the field Sunday. The wide receiver has finally started to mix into the offense after recovering from the torn ACL he suffered in the Bills' 27-24 win over the Jaguars in the 2025 AFC wild-card round.

inj_report.long: Allen played 14 offensive snaps behind Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) and Chris Rodriguez, and Tuten ended up aggravating his ankle issue in the defeat. If Tuten needs to miss time, Allen could see elevated snaps behind Rodriguez, though Ameer Abdullah also is an option for the Jaguars out of the backfield. Ultimately, Allen is much likelier than not to remain irrelevant in fantasy.

inj_report.short: Watkins brought in his lone target for 19 yards during the 49ers' 35-10 win over the Vikings on Sunday.
inj_report.long: Watkins' 28 offensive snaps were tied with Deebo Samuel for second most among 49ers wide receivers behind Keenan Allen (31) and ahead of Mike Evans (23). Watkins has played at least 50 percent of San Francisco's offensive snaps in each of the team's last five games, but the second-year pro is stuck in a complementary role on offense behind Evans, Allen, Samuel, tight end George Kittle and running back Christian McCaffrey. The 49ers travel back home for a critical Week 12 tilt against the Seahawks on Nov. 29.

inj_report.short: Lambert-Smith (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Jets.
inj_report.long: With Ladd McConkey (back) active, Lambert-Smith will be a healthy scratch for Sunday's contest. Lambert-Smith's next opportunity to suit up is Week 12 against the Patriots on Nov. 29, although his path to playing time is limited unless there is an injury in front of him on the Chargers' wide receiver depth chart.

He was signed to the Vikings' 53-man roster Wednesday to give the team more depth at wide receiver while Jordan Addison recovers from a thumb injury. Jones figures to be limited to a rotational role on offense while serving as a contributor on special teams.

inj_report.short: Allen caught two of four targets for 41 yards during Sunday's 34-7 win over the Cardinals.
inj_report.long: Allen was able to reel in multiple passes for the second straight week after having done so only twice in the team's first eight games of the year. The wide receiver played 16 offensive snaps which ranked sixth at his position behind Xavier Worthy (47), Rashee Rice (32), Jalen Royals (24), Andrew Armstrong (20) and Josh Downs (17). As a result of the depth of the WR room in Kansas City, Allen will remain a hard fantasy option to trust Thursday versus the Bills.

inj_report.short: Koziol went without a target while playing four of the Jaguars' 72 snaps on offense in Sunday's 23-18 loss to the Giants.
inj_report.long: The rookie fifth-round pick saw his streak of three straight games with a reception come to an end and also had his snap count decline for the fourth week in a row. Koziol ranked fourth in playing time among Jacksonville tight ends, marking the first time since Week 3 that he had played behind Quintin Morris (11 snaps Sunday).

inj_report.short: Adkins recorded a three-yard reception on two targets in Sunday's 38-24 win over the Raiders.
inj_report.long: Adkins was on the field for 30 of the Broncos' 73 snaps on offense, with his 41 percent share representing a season-high mark. The fourth-year tight end out of South Carolina has mainly served as a blocking specialist for Denver, having thus far been limited to a 7-47-3 receiving line on nine targets to go with a six-yard carry through 10 appearances on the season.

inj_report.short: Quitoriano played all 13 of his snaps on special teams in Sunday's 34-7 loss to the Chiefs.
inj_report.long: Since coming out of nowhere to post two receiving touchdowns in his Cardinals debut back in Week 5 against the Lions, Quitoriano has fallen out of the mix for playing time on offense. After the two-score effort, Quitoriano logged double-digit snaps on offense in four straight contests, but he drew just one target over that stretch. In the subsequent two games, Quitoriano has played just three total snaps on offense while Trey McBride, Elijah Higgins and Hunter Long have been prioritized ahead of him at tight end.

inj_report.short: The Browns designated Sanders (hip) for return from injured reserve Tuesday.
inj_report.long: Cleveland elected to open Sanders' practice window following their Week 11 bye, giving the team up to 21 days to evaluate him for a return to the 53-man roster. Before landing on IR on Oct. 13 due to a hip issue, Sanders carried nine times for 43 yards and added 11 receptions for 74 yards on 12 targets over five contests. He'll likely slot in behind Quinshon Judkins and Dylan Sampson on the depth chart at running back once he's activated.

inj_report.long: Sinnott gave the Commanders a lead just before halftime when he reeled in a one-yard touchdown from Jayden Daniels. It was his first TD of the season and the third of his career. Sinnott's four grabs came out of nowhere, as he'd logged just one catch on two targets through his first eight games of the season. He also ranked third among Washington tight ends Thursday with 24 offensive snaps -- behind Chig Okonkwo (41) and John Bates (28) -- so fantasy managers probably don't need to go rushing to the waiver wire to pick him up. With that said, Sinnott may have earned himself more opportunities with Thursday's effort.

inj_report.short: Kacmarek went without a target while logging 21 of 57 snaps on offense in Sunday's 26-9 loss to the Bills.
inj_report.long: After drawing at least one target in each of the previous three games, Kacmarek failed to draw a look from quarterback Kyle McCord, who connected with seven different pass catchers on the day. Kacmarek ran routes on just six of his 21 snaps, as the Dolphins continue to utilize him mainly as a blocker when he's on the field.

He ran routes on just nine of his 29 snaps in Week 11, with Yurosek mainly serving as a blocker during his time on the field.

Latu will likely see his opportunities take a hit if Kincaid makes it back for a Thursday matchup with the Chiefs in Week 12.

inj_report.long: Thomas had the opportunity to step into the TE2 role behind Michael Mayer on Sunday due to the absence of Brock Bowers (ankle/quadriceps). Thomas' 35 offensive snaps were his most of the season, and he made his lone target from Fernando Mendoza count, with the duo connecting on a 19-yard touchdown pass late in the third quarter to tie the game up at 17-17. Thomas has seven catches on as many targets for 92 yards and two touchdowns through 11 regular-season games, although he would revert to being the No. 3 tight end in Week 12 against the Browns on Nov. 29 if Bowers is cleared to return for that contest.

inj_report.long: The loose ball was recovered by the Steelers, and Pittsburgh's offense turned that takeaway into a 40-yard field goal by Chris Boswell four plays later. It ended up being the only touch of the game for Blue, who played all 11 of his snaps on special teams. There's an outside chance he sees some involvement on offense against the Cowboys on Thanksgiving Day, but that will depend on the availability of both Saquon Barkley (neck/illness) and Will Shipley (foot/illness).

inj_report.short: Etienne rushed six times for 29 yards, caught one pass for seven yards, logged 36 kick return yards and eight punt return yards in the Panthers' 35-33 win over the Ravens on Sunday.
inj_report.long: Etienne did it all in Week 11 while only playing 10 offensive snaps and nine special-teams snaps. Despite the low snap counts, the running back influenced many areas of the box score. Etienne continues to be the reserve option behind bell-cow back Chuba Hubbard, who continues to amass carries and touchdowns for the Panthers offense.

inj_report.long: Though he's been active for each of the Bears' last three games in the wake of Cole Kmet's season-ending knee injury, Carlson remains well behind Colston Loveland and Sam Roush in the pecking order at tight end. Carlson has yet to draw a target and has now played more snaps on special teams than offense in the past two contests.

inj_report.short: Lance failed to catch his only target and added 47 yards as a kick returner during Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Bears.
inj_report.long: Lance was unable to reel in a deep pass from quarterback Tyler Shough in the first quarter, and he didn't get another look the rest of the game. The wide receiver was on the field for 21 offensive snaps, ranking fourth at his position behind Devaughn Vele (64), Chris Olave (62) and Jordyn Tyson (36) in the contest. Lance will continue to be primarily a special-teams asset for New Orleans moving forward, making him an unattractive option for fantasy managers.

inj_report.long: Wetjen has operated as the Steelers' top returner on both kickoffs and punts this season. However, with Roman Wilson back from injured reserve and Max Hurleman elevated from the practice squad to the active roster, Wetjen will be a healthy scratch Sunday for the first time this season. inj_report.short: Ahmed reverted to the Bears' practice squad Monday, according to the NFL's official transaction log.
inj_report.long: The running back was elevated from the practice squad Saturday ahead of Sunday's game against New Orleans, and he carried the ball six times for 33 yards across 10 offensive snaps. Ahmed saw action late in the third quarter and into the fourth, after Roschon Johnson exited the game with an ankle injury in the first quarter. Both are behind D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai on the depth chart.

inj_report.short: Rivers rushed 15 times for 81 yards in Sunday's 34-6 win over the Cardinals.
inj_report.long: Amazingly, all 15 of Rivers' carries came on the Rams' final drive of the game, where they ran 17 plays to kill the final 12 minutes and 15 seconds of the clock. Rivers rushed 15 straight times before Matthew Stafford performed a pair of kneel-downs to end the game. It will be interesting to see if Rivers' efficiency was enough to earn him more carries before garbage time moving forward, especially after Kyren Williams looked stuck in the mud against Arizona, rushing 12 times for just 23 yards. For now, Rivers is simply a name to keep an eye on over the next couple of weeks, with the Rams wanting to lean on the run due to all of their high-profile pass-catching injuries.

inj_report.short: Lock completed 14 of 17 passes for 240 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions and logged six carries for 20 yards during Sunday's 21-13 victory in Las Vegas.
inj_report.long: Lock took advantage of having WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba at his disposal, targeting him 10 times, one of which resulted in a 71-yard TD connection. Moreover, Lock also hooked up with Cooper Kupp on a sliding 34-yard touchdown, marking his second multi-TD outing in four appearances (three starts) this season. There's an expectation that Seahawks No. 1 QB Sam Darnold (quadriceps) returns from a two-game absence after the team's Week 11 bye, but until he receives a clean bill of health, Lock has a chance to be under center on the road against the 49ers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

inj_report.short: The Ravens believe "there's a chance" that Jackson (thumb) could return for their Week 16 matchup with the Browns, assuming all goes well in his recovery from right thumb surgery, Dan Graziano of ESPN.com reports.
inj_report.long: Last Friday, head coach Jesse Minter announced that Jackson was facing a projected recovery timeline of 6-to-10 weeks after requiring a procedure to address a broken and dislocated thumb. A Week 16 return would be right up against the short end of that timeline, so if Jackson has shown notable improvement by that point, he could push to play if the 4-6 Ravens haven't faded from the playoff picture. While Jackson remains sidelined for at least a few more weeks, the Ravens will entrust trade-deadline acquisition Jacoby Brissett to direct the offense.

inj_report.short: Adams (hamstring) has an "outside chance" to return from injured reserve for the Rams' Week 13 matchup with the Chiefs but is more likely to be activated around mid-December, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
inj_report.long: The Rams have seemingly discounted the possibility of Adams coming off IR for a Wednesday matchup with the Packers in Week 12, while a Week 13 return is more plausible but still sounds like a "long shot," according to Rapoport. Instead, the Rams' Week 14 game against the 49ers on Dec. 13 would appear to be the most realistic target for Adams' return, especially since Los Angeles will effectively have a "mini-bye" ahead of that contest following its Thursday night matchup with Kansas City on Dec. 3. Whenever he's reinstated from IR, Adams should be in store for heavy target shares in the Rams' remaining games after star wideout Puka Nacua (knee) underwent season-ending MCL surgery earlier this week.

inj_report.short: Taylor completed one of two pass attempts for three yards in Sunday's 30-10 loss to the Vikings.
inj_report.long: Down 20 points with four minutes remaining in the fourth quarter and with starting quarterback Jordan Love having already taken eight sacks on the afternoon, the Packers opted to turn to Taylor to direct the offense for their final possession of the day. All three of Taylor's appearances on the season have now come late in blowout wins or losses, and his opportunities are likely to remain limited to garbage-time situations so long as Love is healthy.

inj_report.short: Rams head coach Sean McVay said Monday that Ferguson (hamstring) won't be activated from injured reserve this season and will require surgery to address the ankle injury he aggravated in Week 3, Stu Jackson of the team's official site reports.
inj_report.long: Ferguson initially seemed to be making good progress in his recovery from the ankle injury, as the Rams elected to open his 21-day evaluation window Nov. 4. However, Ferguson's activation from IR was delayed after he strained his hamstring shortly after he resumed working out, and he hasn't practiced in more than two weeks. Rather than the hamstring issue, McVay noted that the ankle injury remained the greater concern for Ferguson, who didn't improve as well as the Rams had hoped and now will require a procedure. Los Angeles will have to proceed without two of its top pass catchers for the remainder of the season, as Puka Nacua recently underwent an MCL surgery that entails an estimated 4-to-5-month recovery timeline.

inj_report.long: McGowan went down with the injury while returning a kickoff in the first half of the Week 11 loss. The rookie seventh-round pick had been solidified as the top backup to starting running back Jonathan Taylor, but DJ Giddens now is positioned to serve as Taylor's main understudy for however long McGowan is sidelined. McGowan can be safely ruled out for the Week 12 game against the Giants, though a Week 13 bye could help the 25-year-old back avoid additional absences beyond that.

inj_report.short: Nacua (knee/toe) is expected to be sidelined 4-to-5 months after undergoing surgery Tuesday to repair his right MCL, which means he won't be on track to return at any point during the playoffs, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
inj_report.long: Nacua is also dealing with a PCL sprain and turf toe, but the only procedure he required was for his MCL. With a firmer 4-to-5-month timeline now in place for the star wideout, he'll be done for the season while the Rams look to others to help fill the massive void in their receiver corps. Davante Adams (hamstring) should eventually take on a heavy target share, but he's also on injured reserve and isn't expected to return until at least Week 13. That leaves Konata Mumpfield, CJ Daniels, Tutu Atwell and Xavier Smith as the current healthy wideouts on the team's 53-man roster ahead of next Wednesday's tilt versus the Packers. Nacua, who is in the final year of his rookie deal, is slated to become a free agent in March.

inj_report.long: J.J. McCarthy made his third consecutive start for the Giants, but Winston continued to get sprinkled into the game plan during short-yardage situations. If Jacobs is forced to miss a second consecutive game, Kaleb Johnson and MarShawn Lloyd would be in line to lead the Green Bay rushing attack for another week.

inj_report.short: For now, Maye -- who suffered a fractured right fibula during a Week 10 loss to the Lions -- remains on the Patriots' 53-man roster rather than injured reserve, with coach Mike Vrabel citing the "balance" the team is hoping to strike with regard to managing its remaining designated to return from IR slots, Mike Reiss of ESPN.com reports.
inj_report.long: Per Reiss, teams are limited to eight players that can be designated to return from the list over the course of the regular season, and the Patriots are close to using them all. "Right now, he's not on injured reserve," Vrabel said Monday. "He's on the active roster, so that's where it is today. I think that those things are obviously fluid. But we want to try to give him every opportunity that we can to be back at some point in time. I don't know when that will be; I'm not sure. But also, try to manage the roster and do what we need to do to try to win each week." On Sunday, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported that Maye was on track to miss at least six weeks, a timetable that suggests, in a best-case scenario, the QB could make a push for a late-season return or for the postseason, should New England qualify. Heading into a Week 12 game against the Chargers, Tommy DeVito is slated to work as the team's starter, with rookie Behren Morton on hand as his backup. Additionally, there's the possibility that the team considers Daniel Jones -- who the Colts let go Friday -- as an alternative, but Vrabel told Reiss that in the short term at least, adding another signal-caller is not something that's being planned.
